title: First-Token Attraction in Mamba Dynamics
claim: Simulated trajectories show the first element of a sequence converges to discrete attractors and pulls later elements to the same points.
layout: 3 panels side-by-side, each a 3D sphere with axes and sub-captions
description: Three 3D unit-sphere plots sit side by side, each with x, y, z axes and black latitude/longitude grid lines. Colored curves trace token trajectories across the sphere surface. Small red dots mark the random starting points, and large red dots mark the attractors, which sit at coordinate unit vectors. Panel (a) shows the first-token trajectories from 100 random initializations. Most curves fan out and converge to a few red attractor points. Panel (b) shows one sequence of 32 tokens with time-independent parameters. The smooth curves converge toward a single point on the x axis. Panel (c) shows one sequence of 16 tokens with time-dependent parameters. The jagged, noisy paths cluster near the top and bottom poles. Sub-captions under each panel give the setup and the convergence result in math notation. The eye goes first to the large red attractor dots and the dense multicolor curves.
caption: Simulated trajectories of dynamical system (6) with random parameters. The initial points (denoted by small red points in (a) and (b)) are sampled via a uniform distribution on the sphere. In these settings, the first token converges to discrete attractors at the big red points (mostly coordinate unit vectors ±ed) and draws subsequent tokens toward the same points, producing clusters and illustrating the attention sink effect.
abstract: We study token dynamics in deep Mamba models, with a particular focus on the attracting role of the first token. Unlike attention mechanisms, where token interactions are governed by positive scalar coefficients, Mamba dynamics involve full matrix-valued interaction coefficients with no positivity or definiteness guarantees. This structural difference makes Mamba dynamics substantially harder to analyze and prevents the direct application of existing techniques for attention-based models. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a new analytical framework based on a high-dimensional invariant box and a sharp exit-time argument, which together recover an effective form of sign-definiteness. Using this framework, we characterize the possible limit points of token trajectories and prove explicit exponential convergence rates. Our analysis reveals that the first token has privileged dynamics: its limiting direction attracts subsequent tokens, inducing token clustering and attention-sink phenomena in deep Mamba models. We further show that this attraction mechanism extends to broader sequence dynamics, including state-space models, causal attention, and classical time-series models. Experiments on Falcon-Mamba-7B validate our predictions, showing that concentration on the first token increases with depth and dominates in later layers.
